vocabulary.example: I need to find a charging point to recharge my electric car.
vocabulary.translation: 我需要找一个充电桩给我的电动汽车充电。

vocabulary.entry: petrol car /ˈpetrəl kɑː(r)/ n. 汽油车
vocabulary.example: The sale of new petrol cars will be banned in the country by 2030.
vocabulary.translation: 该国将于2030年起禁止销售新的汽油车。

vocabulary.entry: diesel car /ˈdiːzl kɑː(r)/ n. 柴油车
vocabulary.example: Diesel cars are known for their higher fuel efficiency but more emissions.
vocabulary.translation: 柴油车以燃油效率较高但排放量更大而闻名。

vocabulary.entry: offset /ˈɒfset/ v. 抵消（排放量）
vocabulary.example: We can offset our carbon footprint by planting trees.
vocabulary.translation: 我们可以通过植树来抵消自己的碳足迹。

vocabulary.entry: hectare /ˈhekteə(r)/ n. 公顷
vocabulary.example: The forest covers an area of 500 hectares.

vocabulary.entry: pledge /pledʒ/ v. 承诺；保证
vocabulary.example: The company has pledged to reduce its emissions by 50% by 2030.
vocabulary.translation: 该公司承诺到2030年将排放量减少50%。

vocabulary.entry: weigh up /weɪ ʌp/ v. 权衡；考量
vocabulary.example: We need to weigh up the pros and cons before making a decision.
vocabulary.translation: 做决定前，我们需要权衡利弊。

vocabulary.entry: inaction /ɪnˈækʃn/ n. 不作为；无行动
vocabulary.example: Inaction on climate change will lead to severe consequences.
vocabulary.translation: 在气候变化问题上的不作为将导致严重后果。

vocabulary.entry: renewable energy /rɪˈnjuːəbl ˈenədʒi/ n. 可再生能源
vocabulary.example: Solar and wind power are two common types of renewable energy.
vocabulary.translation: 太阳能和风能是两种常见的可再生能源。

vocabulary.entry: carbon footprint /ˈkɑːbən ˈfʊtprɪnt/ n. 碳足迹
vocabulary.example: We should try to reduce our carbon footprint by saving energy.
vocabulary.translation: 我们应该通过节约能源来减少自己的碳足迹。

vocabulary.entry: extreme weather event /ɪkˈstriːm ˈweðə ɪˈvent/ n. 极端天气事件
vocabulary.example: Hurricanes and droughts are examples of extreme weather events.
vocabulary.translation: 飓风和干旱都属于极端天气事件。

vocabulary.entry: environmental policy /ɪnˌvaɪrənˈmentl ˈpɒləsi/ n. 环境政策
vocabulary.example: The government's new environmental policy has received widespread support.
vocabulary.translation: 政府的新环境政策获得了广泛支持。

vocabulary.entry: energy efficiency /ˈenədʒi ɪˈfɪʃnsi/ n. 能源效率
vocabulary.example: Improving energy efficiency is an effective way to cut emissions.
vocabulary.translation: 提高能源效率是减排的有效途径。

vocabulary.entry: global cooperation /ˈɡləʊbl kəʊˌɒpəˈreɪʃn/ n. 全球合作
vocabulary.example: Global cooperation is essential to address climate change.
vocabulary.translation: 全球合作对于应对气候变化至关重要。

sentences.english: We are all aware of the effect greenhouse gas emissions is having on our planet and the efforts needed to tackle climate change.
sentences.chinese: 我们都清楚温室气体排放对地球造成的影响，也明白应对气候变化需要付出怎样的努力。

sentences.english: Most of us are doing our bit to minimise our impact on the environment, but despite our collective effort, are we doing enough to achieve net zero by 2050?
sentences.chinese: 大多数人都在尽自己的一份力，减少对环境的影响，但即便我们共同努力，要在2050年实现净零排放目标，我们目前所做的真的足够吗？

sentences.english: Net zero means not adding to the amount of greenhouse gases in the atmosphere.
sentences.chinese: 净零排放是指不再向大气中新增温室气体。

sentences.english: Many countries are doing their bit by changing how they generate and use power, thereby cutting carbon dioxide output.
sentences.chinese: 许多国家正通过改变能源的生产和使用方式来尽一份力，从而减少二氧化碳的排放量。

sentences.english: And they announced what further steps they were going to take at the recent COP26 summit in Glasgow.
sentences.chinese: 在最近于格拉斯哥举办的第26届联合国气候变化大会上，各国公布了后续将要采取的举措。

sentences.english: In the UK, the government has been setting out its plans to achieve net zero by 2050.
sentences.chinese: 英国政府已出台了2050年实现净零排放的相关计划。

sentences.english: It’s recently announced an end date for the sale of gas boilers, which are used for heating homes. The idea is to replace them with heat pumps. It’s offering homeowners grants of up to £5,000 to get them installed.
sentences.chinese: 该国近期宣布了家用燃气锅炉的截止销售时间，计划用热泵取而代之，同时还向房主提供最高5000英镑的补贴，用于安装热泵。

sentences.english: Another initiative in the UK is a big push towards electric vehicles. There are to be financial incentives for car manufacturers, and more charging points are to be installed in streets. And there’s to be a ban on the sale of new petrol and diesel cars by 2030.
sentences.chinese: 英国的另一项举措是大力推广电动汽车，不仅为汽车制造商提供财务补贴，还将在街道上增设更多充电桩，并且计划在2030年起禁止销售新的汽油车和柴油车。

sentences.english: But not all emissions can be reduced to zero, so those remaining will have to be compensated for, or offset.
sentences.chinese: 但并非所有排放都能降至零，因此剩余的排放量必须通过抵消手段来处理。

sentences.english: One way to do this is to plant thousands of trees, which are good at absorbing carbon dioxide.
sentences.chinese: 其中一种方法是大规模植树造林，树木善于吸收二氧化碳。

sentences.english: The UK government has pledged to plant 30,000 hectares of trees a year by 2025.
sentences.chinese: 英国政府承诺，到2025年每年将植树3万公顷。

sentences.english: There are other ideas too, but what’s certain is this will cost money.
sentences.chinese: 当然还有其他的减排思路，但可以肯定的是，实现净零排放需要投入大量资金。

sentences.english: The CBI’s Tom Thackray told the BBC that “those costs have to be weighed up against the cost of inaction.”
sentences.chinese: 英国工业联合会的汤姆·撒克雷在接受BBC采访时表示：“我们必须权衡这些投入与不作为所付出的代价。”

sentences.english: Whether the UK, or anyone else, reaches net zero remains to be seen.
sentences.chinese: 英国或其他任何国家能否如期实现净零排放，尚有待观察。

sentences.english: And there’s some doubt about how this can be accurately measured anyway.
sentences.chinese: 此外，关于如何准确测算净零排放，目前也存在一些争议。

sentences.english: But it’s generally recognised that a global effort is needed to tackle climate change.
sentences.chinese: 但人们普遍认为，应对气候变化需要全球共同努力。

sentences.english: Therefore, net zero targets only make sense if every other country is moving in the same direction.
sentences.chinese: 因此，只有当所有国家都朝着同一个方向迈进时，净零排放目标才有实际意义。

title: Why do people like horror films
titleChinese: 人们为什么爱看恐怖片？
paragraphs: What’s your favourite genre of film? For many people who love being petrified, or scared out of their wits, by jump scares that answer will be horror. Whether it’s splatter films, wastelands in the apocalypse, monsters like demons, zombies, vampires, werewolves or phantoms, there’s something to suit everyone’s taste. But just why do people enjoy watching these terrifying films?

First off, being scared can give us a rush of adrenaline. The heart starts pumping, making these films exhilarating. But the fact you’re actually at home safe on the sofa makes the experience of being frightened all the more enjoyable because what’s happening to the characters on the screen is far removed from your experience of being in your living room eating popcorn. It feels more thrilling.

Coltan Scrivner, a PhD candidate in the Department of Comparative Human Development at The University of Chicago, argues that people who watch horror films learn how to regulate their anxiety. A study that he co-authored found that horror fans exhibited greater resilience during the early stages on the Covid-19 pandemic than those who didn’t.

Also, some horror fans think they could survive the events on screen. That gives those viewers a sense of superiority. We often mock the typical tropes of horror films. Why do they try to escape the masked killer by running upstairs and confining themselves? The characters often make terrible decisions that lead to their deaths – decisions we as viewers believe we wouldn’t make.

So, whether it’s to help people regulate their anxiety, be thrilled by getting scared, or to feel superior mocking the decisions of the characters, there are many reasons people love watching horror films – and if they really scare you, maybe it’s best to watch them with the lights on.

vocabulary.entry: genre /ˈʒɒnrə/ n. 类型；体裁
vocabulary.example: Science fiction is a popular genre that explores futuristic concepts.
vocabulary.translation: 科幻是一种探索未来概念的热门体裁。

vocabulary.entry: petrified /ˈpetrɪfaɪd/ adj. 吓得僵住的；石化的
vocabulary.example: She was petrified when she heard a loud noise outside her window.
vocabulary.translation: 听到窗外的巨响时，她吓得僵住了。

vocabulary.entry: jump scare /dʒʌmp skeə(r)/ n. （影视中的）突然惊吓

vocabulary.translation: 这部电影里满是让人尖叫的突然惊吓桥段。

vocabulary.entry: splatter film /ˈsplætə fɪlm/ n. 血腥暴力片
vocabulary.example: The splatter film is not suitable for audiences with a weak stomach.
vocabulary.translation: 这部血腥暴力片不适合肠胃敏感的观众观看。

vocabulary.entry: apocalypse /əˈpɒkəlɪps/ n. 末日；世界毁灭
vocabulary.example: The novel depicts a post-apocalypse world where resources are scarce.
vocabulary.translation: 这部小说描绘了一个资源匮乏的后末日世界。

vocabulary.entry: demon /ˈdiːmən/ n. 恶魔；恶鬼

vocabulary.translation: 传说有一只恶魔在林间的古堡里作祟。

vocabulary.entry: zombie /ˈzɒmbi/ n. 僵尸

vocabulary.translation: 这部电影里，一种病毒把大部分人类变成了食肉僵尸。

vocabulary.entry: vampire /ˈvæmpaɪə(r)/ n. 吸血鬼
vocabulary.example: The vampire can only come out at night and avoids sunlight.
vocabulary.translation: 吸血鬼只能在夜间出没，并且惧怕阳光。

vocabulary.entry: werewolf /ˈweəwʊlf/ n. 狼人
vocabulary.example: The werewolf transforms from a human on full moon nights.
vocabulary.translation: 每逢月圆之夜，这个狼人就会从人形变身。

vocabulary.entry: phantom /ˈfæntəm/ n. 幽灵；幻影
vocabulary.example: A phantom of a little girl is said to walk the halls of the old school.
vocabulary.translation: 据说有个小女孩的幽灵在这所旧学校的走廊里游荡。

vocabulary.entry: adrenaline /əˈdrenəlɪn/ n. 肾上腺素
vocabulary.example: Skydiving gives you a huge adrenaline rush.
vocabulary.translation: 跳伞会让你肾上腺素急剧飙升。

vocabulary.entry: exhilarating /ɪɡˈzɪləreɪtɪŋ/ adj. 令人兴奋的；使人振奋的
vocabulary.example: The roller coaster ride was an exhilarating experience for the children.
vocabulary.translation: 坐过山车对孩子们来说是一次令人兴奋的体验。

vocabulary.entry: far removed /fɑː rɪˈmuːvd/ adj. 相距甚远的；毫不相干的
vocabulary.example: His lifestyle is far removed from the poverty he knew as a child.
vocabulary.translation: 他现在的生活方式和小时候经历的贫困相去甚远。

vocabulary.entry: thrilling /ˈθrɪlɪŋ/ adj. 令人激动的；扣人心弦的
vocabulary.example: The last ten minutes of the match were the most thrilling part.
vocabulary.translation: 比赛的最后十分钟是最扣人心弦的部分。

vocabulary.entry: regulate /ˈreɡjuleɪt/ v. 调节；控制
vocabulary.example: It is important to regulate your breathing when you feel anxious.
vocabulary.translation: 感到焦虑时，调节呼吸至关重要。

vocabulary.entry: anxiety /æŋˈzaɪəti/ n. 焦虑；忧虑
vocabulary.example: She suffers from anxiety when she has to speak in public.
vocabulary.translation: 她在公开场合发言时会感到焦虑。

vocabulary.entry: resilience /rɪˈzɪliəns/ n. 韧性；适应力
vocabulary.example: The child showed great resilience after losing both parents.
vocabulary.translation: 这个孩子在失去双亲后表现出了极强的韧性。

vocabulary.entry: superiority /suːˌpɪəriˈɒrəti/ n. 优越感；优越性
vocabulary.example: He has a sense of superiority because of his expensive education.
vocabulary.translation: 他因为接受过昂贵的教育而有一种优越感。

vocabulary.entry: mock /mɒk/ v. 嘲笑；嘲弄
vocabulary.example: The students mocked his strange accent when he first arrived.
vocabulary.translation: 他刚来的时候，同学们嘲笑他奇怪的口音。

vocabulary.translation: “英雄之旅”是许多冒险故事中常见的套路。

vocabulary.entry: masked killer /mɑːskt ˈkɪlə(r)/ n. 蒙面杀手

vocabulary.translation: 电影里的蒙面杀手会在每个犯罪现场留下一个神秘符号。

vocabulary.entry: confine /kənˈfaɪn/ v. 禁闭；限制
vocabulary.example: The prisoner was confined to a small cell for ten years.
vocabulary.translation: 这名囚犯被关在狭小的牢房里长达十年。

vocabulary.translation: 把所有钱都投到那个高风险项目里是个糟糕的决定。

vocabulary.translation: 这位病人表现出了发烧和头痛的症状。

sentences.english: What’s your favourite genre of film?

sentences.english: Whether it’s splatter films, wastelands in the apocalypse, monsters like demons, zombies, vampires, werewolves or phantoms, there’s something to suit everyone’s taste.
sentences.chinese: 无论是血腥暴力片、末日荒原题材，还是恶魔、僵尸、吸血鬼、狼人、幽灵这类怪物形象，恐怖片的题材丰富多样，总能满足不同人的喜好。

sentences.english: But just why do people enjoy watching these terrifying films?
sentences.chinese: 但人们究竟为什么会喜欢看这些令人毛骨悚然的电影呢？

sentences.english: First off, being scared can give us a rush of adrenaline. The heart starts pumping, making these films exhilarating.
sentences.chinese: 首先，恐惧的感觉能让我们肾上腺素飙升，心跳加速，让看这类电影的过程变得刺激十足。

sentences.english: But the fact you’re actually at home safe on the sofa makes the experience of being frightened all the more enjoyable because what’s happening to the characters on the screen is far removed from your experience of being in your living room eating popcorn. It feels more thrilling.
sentences.chinese: 而实际上你正安安稳稳地坐在家里的沙发上，这种安全的环境会让恐惧感变得更加有趣——毕竟屏幕上角色的遭遇，和你在客厅吃着爆米花的现实生活相去甚远，也因此更惊险刺激。

sentences.english: Coltan Scrivner, a PhD candidate in the Department of Comparative Human Development at The University of Chicago, argues that people who watch horror films learn how to regulate their anxiety.
sentences.chinese: 芝加哥大学比较人类发展系的博士生科尔坦·斯克里夫纳认为，观看恐怖片能让人学会调节自身的焦虑情绪。

sentences.english: A study that he co-authored found that horror fans exhibited greater resilience during the early stages on the Covid-19 pandemic than those who didn’t.
sentences.chinese: 他参与撰写的一项研究发现，在新冠疫情初期，恐怖片爱好者比不看恐怖片的人表现出更强的心理韧性。

sentences.english: Also, some horror fans think they could survive the events on screen. That gives those viewers a sense of superiority.
sentences.chinese: 此外，部分恐怖片爱好者认为自己能在电影里的绝境中活下来，这种想法会让他们产生一种优越感。

sentences.english: We often mock the typical tropes of horror films. Why do they try to escape the masked killer by running upstairs and confining themselves?
sentences.chinese: 我们常常会吐槽恐怖片的经典套路：为什么角色要往楼上跑，把自己困在那里躲避蒙面杀手？

sentences.english: The characters often make terrible decisions that lead to their deaths – decisions we as viewers believe we wouldn’t make.
sentences.chinese: 片中角色总是做出致命的糟糕决定，而观众们都觉得换作是自己，绝不会犯这样的错。

sentences.english: So, whether it’s to help people regulate their anxiety, be thrilled by getting scared, or to feel superior mocking the decisions of the characters, there are many reasons people love watching horror films – and if they really scare you, maybe it’s best to watch them with the lights on.
sentences.chinese: 所以，无论是为了调节焦虑情绪、享受惊吓带来的刺激感，还是为了吐槽角色的愚蠢决定而获得优越感，人们喜欢看恐怖片的原因多种多样。不过如果恐怖片真的把你吓得不轻，或许还是开着灯看比较好。

title: Surviving the winter blues
titleChinese: 撑过冬季带来的忧郁情绪
paragraphs: It’s the middle of winter, and the prospect of warm sunny days is a long way off. For some of us, it’s the most depressing time of year, where daylight is limited and the weather is often miserable – this is when the winter blues set in. So what can be done to lift our spirits?

The shorter days and longer nights can make us feel down, and that can cause us to eat more and exercise less. Some fear loneliness and isolation during the long dark months. Those people who suffer this seasonal mood swing more seriously are described as having seasonal affective disorder – or SAD for short. It’s a type of depression with a seasonal pattern caused by a lack of light and is thought to affect the part of the brain that rules sleep, appetite, mood and activity levels.

Jenny Scott-Thompson is one person who was diagnosed with SAD. She told the BBC: “I struggled with periods of exhaustion and misery that seemed out of proportion to what was going on in my life.” She was prescribed light therapy, which involved sitting in front of a light box. As well as going outside during daylight hours, this is believed to help anyone who is affected by the winter gloom.

Although having more light is an obvious cure, antidepressants can help those with more severe depression by artificially elevating the amount of serotonin in the brain. But this isn’t suitable for everyone, and many of us can try to just alter our mindset. Clinical psychologist Laura Keyes says, “it can be helpful to think about how to adapt your eating and exercise patterns to the change of season, just as this happens in nature with plants and animals adapting.”

It might sound easier said than done, but accepting winter and thinking positively may energise us. Writing for The BBC Social website, Esther De La Ford asks “What if we explored what this phase of winter has to offer us, instead of grieving those things that it is taking away?” She suggests we use this time for rest, reflection, slowing down, stillness and renewal. Maybe this might stop us longing for summer?

vocabulary.entry: prospect /ˈprɒspekt/ n. 前景；展望
vocabulary.example: The prospect of a long holiday makes her excited.
vocabulary.translation: 长假的前景让她很兴奋。

vocabulary.entry: daylight /ˈdeɪlaɪt/ n. 日光；白昼
vocabulary.example: We should make the most of the daylight to finish the work.
vocabulary.translation: 我们应该充分利用日光完成这项工作。

vocabulary.entry: misery /ˈmɪzəri/ n. 痛苦；悲惨境遇
vocabulary.example: The old man lived in misery for most of his life.
vocabulary.translation: 这位老人大半生都过着悲惨的生活。

vocabulary.entry: winter blues /ˈwɪntə bluːz/ n. 冬日抑郁情绪
vocabulary.example: Many people suffer from the winter blues when days get shorter.
vocabulary.translation: 白昼变短的时候，很多人会陷入冬日抑郁情绪。

vocabulary.entry: isolation /ˌaɪsəˈleɪʃn/ n. 隔绝；孤立
vocabulary.example: The prisoner was kept in isolation for three days.
vocabulary.translation: 这名囚犯被单独关押了三天。

vocabulary.entry: seasonal mood swing /ˈsiːzənl muːd swɪŋ/ n. 季节性情绪波动
vocabulary.example: Seasonal mood swing is common among people living in high latitudes.
vocabulary.translation: 季节性情绪波动在高纬度地区的人群中很常见。

vocabulary.entry: seasonal affective disorder /ˈsiːzənl əˈfektɪv dɪsˈɔːdə/ n. 季节性情感障碍（SAD）
vocabulary.example: Seasonal affective disorder usually occurs in winter.
vocabulary.translation: 季节性情感障碍通常在冬季发作。

vocabulary.entry: depression /dɪˈpreʃn/ n. 抑郁症；抑郁
vocabulary.example: She has been receiving treatment for depression for six months.
vocabulary.translation: 她已经接受抑郁症治疗六个月了。

vocabulary.entry: exhaustion /ɪɡˈzɔːstʃən/ n. 疲惫；筋疲力尽
vocabulary.example: His exhaustion was obvious after the long journey.
vocabulary.translation: 长途旅行后，他的疲惫显而易见。

vocabulary.entry: out of proportion /aʊt ɒv prəˈpɔːʃn/ adj. 不成比例的；过分的
vocabulary.example: His reaction to the mistake was out of proportion.
vocabulary.translation: 他对这个错误的反应有些过分了。

vocabulary.entry: light therapy /laɪt ˈθerəpi/ n. 光照疗法
vocabulary.example: Light therapy is an effective treatment for SAD.
vocabulary.translation: 光照疗法是治疗季节性情感障碍的有效手段。

vocabulary.entry: light box /laɪt bɒks/ n. 灯箱
vocabulary.example: She sits in front of a light box for 30 minutes every morning.
vocabulary.translation: 她每天早上都会坐在灯箱前30分钟。

vocabulary.entry: gloom /ɡluːm/ n. 阴霾；忧郁
vocabulary.example: The winter gloom made her feel listless all day.
vocabulary.translation: 冬日的阴霾让她一整天都无精打采。

vocabulary.entry: antidepressant /ˌæntidɪˈpresnt/ n. 抗抑郁药
vocabulary.example: The doctor prescribed an antidepressant to help her sleep better.
vocabulary.translation: 医生开了一种抗抑郁药，帮她改善睡眠。

vocabulary.entry: serotonin /ˌserəˈtəʊnɪn/ n. 血清素
vocabulary.example: Serotonin plays an important role in regulating mood.
vocabulary.translation: 血清素在调节情绪方面起着重要作用。

vocabulary.entry: mindset /ˈmaɪndset/ n. 心态；思维模式
vocabulary.example: It's time to change your mindset and look at the problem differently.
vocabulary.translation: 是时候改变心态，换个角度看问题了。

vocabulary.entry: clinical psychologist /ˈklɪnɪkl saɪˈkɒlədʒɪst/ n. 临床心理学家
vocabulary.example: The clinical psychologist gave her some advice on managing stress.
vocabulary.translation: 这位临床心理学家给了她一些应对压力的建议。

vocabulary.entry: pattern /ˈpætn/ n. 模式；方式
vocabulary.example: She has established a regular pattern of work and rest.
vocabulary.translation: 她已经养成了规律的作息模式。

vocabulary.entry: adapt /əˈdæpt/ v. 适应；调整
vocabulary.example: It took her a while to adapt to the new school.
vocabulary.translation: 她花了一段时间才适应新学校。

vocabulary.entry: energise /ˈenədʒaɪz/ v. 使充满活力；激励
vocabulary.example: A cup of coffee can energise you in the morning.
vocabulary.translation: 早上一杯咖啡能让你充满活力。

vocabulary.entry: phase /feɪz/ n. 阶段；时期
vocabulary.example: The project is now in its final phase.
vocabulary.translation: 这个项目现在处于最后阶段。

vocabulary.entry: grieve /ɡriːv/ v. 惋惜；悲伤
vocabulary.example: She grieved the loss of her favorite book for days.
vocabulary.translation: 她为丢失了心爱的书惋惜了好几天。

vocabulary.entry: reflection /rɪˈflekʃn/ n. 反思；沉思
vocabulary.example: He spent the weekend in quiet reflection.
vocabulary.translation: 他在安静的沉思中度过了周末。

vocabulary.entry: stillness /ˈstɪlnəs/ n. 宁静；静止
vocabulary.example: She enjoyed the stillness of the forest in the early morning.
vocabulary.translation: 她喜欢清晨森林的宁静。

vocabulary.entry: renewal /rɪˈnjuːəl/ n. 更新；恢复
vocabulary.example: The vacation gave her a sense of renewal and energy.
vocabulary.translation: 这次假期让她感到焕然一新，充满了活力。

sentences.english: It’s the middle of winter, and the prospect of warm sunny days is a long way off.
sentences.chinese: 时值隆冬，暖阳高照的日子还遥遥无期。

sentences.english: For some of us, it’s the most depressing time of year, where daylight is limited and the weather is often miserable – this is when the winter blues set in.
sentences.chinese: 对有些人来说，这是一年中最令人沮丧的时节——白昼短暂，天气也常常阴冷难捱，冬日抑郁情绪也随之而来。

sentences.english: So what can be done to lift our spirits?
sentences.chinese: 那么，我们该如何提振心情呢？

sentences.english: The shorter days and longer nights can make us feel down, and that can cause us to eat more and exercise less.
sentences.chinese: 昼短夜长的环境会让人情绪低落，进而导致暴饮暴食、疏于运动。

sentences.english: Some fear loneliness and isolation during the long dark months.
sentences.chinese: 还有些人会在漫长的黑暗月份里惧怕孤独与隔绝。

sentences.english: Those people who suffer this seasonal mood swing more seriously are described as having seasonal affective disorder – or SAD for short.
sentences.chinese: 那些受这种季节性情绪波动影响更为严重的人，被认为患上了季节性情感障碍，简称SAD。

sentences.english: It’s a type of depression with a seasonal pattern caused by a lack of light and is thought to affect the part of the brain that rules sleep, appetite, mood and activity levels.
sentences.chinese: 这是一种具有季节性特征的抑郁症，由光照不足引发，人们认为其会影响大脑中掌管睡眠、食欲、情绪和活动水平的区域。

sentences.english: Jenny Scott-Thompson is one person who was diagnosed with SAD.
sentences.chinese: 珍妮·斯科特-汤普森就是一位被确诊为SAD的患者。

sentences.english: She told the BBC: “I struggled with periods of exhaustion and misery that seemed out of proportion to what was going on in my life.”
sentences.chinese: 她在接受BBC采访时表示：“我曾长期被疲惫和痛苦困扰，这种状态在我的生活中多到有些过分了。”

sentences.english: She was prescribed light therapy, which involved sitting in front of a light box.
sentences.chinese: 医生为她开具了光照疗法的处方，具体方式是坐在灯箱前接受光照。

sentences.english: As well as going outside during daylight hours, this is believed to help anyone who is affected by the winter gloom.
sentences.chinese: 除了在白天外出活动外，这种疗法也被认为能帮助所有受冬日阴霾影响的人。

sentences.english: Although having more light is an obvious cure, antidepressants can help those with more severe depression by artificially elevating the amount of serotonin in the brain.
sentences.chinese: 虽然增加光照是一种显而易见的缓解方法，但抗抑郁药物也能通过人为提升大脑中的血清素含量，帮助那些抑郁症状较严重的人。

sentences.english: But this isn’t suitable for everyone, and many of us can try to just alter our mindset.
sentences.chinese: 不过这种方法并非适合所有人，我们很多人可以尝试调整自己的心态。

sentences.english: Clinical psychologist Laura Keyes says, “it can be helpful to think about how to adapt your eating and exercise patterns to the change of season, just as this happens in nature with plants and animals adapting.”
sentences.chinese: 临床心理学家劳拉·凯斯说：“思考如何让饮食和运动模式适应季节变化是帮助的，就像自然界中的动植物都会顺应时节调整自身状态一样。”

sentences.english: It might sound easier said than done, but accepting winter and thinking positively may energise us.
sentences.chinese: 这听起来可能说起来容易做起来难，但接纳冬天、保持积极心态，或许能为我们注入活力。

sentences.english: Writing for The BBC Social website, Esther De La Ford asks “What if we explored what this phase of winter has to offer us, instead of grieving those things that it is taking away?”
sentences.chinese: 埃丝特·德拉福特在为BBC社交频道撰稿时提出疑问：“如果我们不去惋惜冬天带走的东西，而是去发掘这个季节能带给我们什么，会怎么样呢？”

sentences.english: She suggests we use this time for rest, reflection, slowing down, stillness and renewal.
sentences.chinese: 她建议我们利用这段时间休息、反思、放慢节奏、享受宁静，完成自我更新。

sentences.english: Maybe this might stop us longing for summer?
sentences.chinese: 或许这样一来，我们就不会那么渴望夏天了。

title: An ageing population
paragraphs: There’s one thing for certain – we’re all getting older. And while the older amongst us may be no spring chickens any more, growing old gracefully is no bad thing. And with age comes wisdom. However, as the world population ages, will there be enough people to replace our younger selves?

A situation where there are more old people than young certainly has an effect on the world. A report by the Pew Research Center says that globally the number of people over 65 years old will triple by 2050, drastically altering some countries’ demographic make-up.

This growing and dependent population means that there is an increased demand for health and social care. Governments will struggle to provide satisfactory pensions, which are ultimately funded by taxes paid by the working population. And long-term, a smaller population of economically-active people may be a problem for companies trying to recruit staff.

Attitudes to an ageing population vary around the world. The Pew Research Center survey found that 87% of Japanese people were most concerned about it, while only 26% of people from the USA were. Here, immigration is helping to boost the younger workforce. Some countries thought the elderly should take care of themselves, while others thought it was the responsibility of the family. Many thought the government should be responsible.

But old age shouldn’t just be seen negatively. Elderly people have knowledge and experience they can pass on. Some have wealth which they can spend, helping the economy. And some help society by doing voluntary or charity work.

Of course, solutions are needed to tackle the issue, and these include increasing the retirement age, encouraging people to save for the future, persuading skilled and educated migrants to fill labour shortages, or even convincing people to have more children.

vocabulary.example: The demographic make-up of the region has changed a lot in the past decade.
vocabulary.translation: 过去十年间，该地区的人口结构发生了很大变化。

vocabulary.entry: dependent population /dɪˈpendənt ˌpɒpjuˈleɪʃn/ n. 受扶养人口

vocabulary.translation: 庞大的受扶养人口可能会给社会保障体系带来压力。

vocabulary.translation: 他从公司退休后，每月都能领取养老金。

vocabulary.entry: economically-active /ˌiːkəˈnɒmɪkli ˈæktɪv/ adj. 有经济活动能力的；劳动适龄的

vocabulary.translation: 劳动适龄人口是税收的主要贡献者。

vocabulary.translation: 这家工厂正面临熟练劳动力短缺的问题。

vocabulary.entry: voluntary work /ˈvɒləntri wɜːk/ n. 志愿工作

vocabulary.translation: 她每个周末都会在当地社区中心做志愿工作。

vocabulary.entry: charity work /ˈtʃærəti wɜːk/ n. 慈善工作

vocabulary.translation: 政府计划逐步提高退休年龄。

vocabulary.translation: 建筑业正面临严重的劳动力短缺问题。

vocabulary.translation: 这家公司的利润在短短一年内增长到了原来的三倍。

vocabulary.translation: 这项新政策彻底改变了人们的日常生活。

title: Humour and resilience
paragraphs: Sometimes life doesn’t seem to play fair. It blindsides you at the most inopportune moments, and even if we can learn to grin and bear the ups and downs, they can take their toll on our psyche. So rather than suffer in silence or let these things get you down, maybe there is another way: what if humour can help you get through the dark times?

According to author and clinician Kristen Lee: “Laughter and tears are both therapeutic – we need both to process such hard times.” But how can we find the tough things that happen funny? Our lives are really serious, often filled with mundane and repetitive activities, whether it’s arbitrary bill paying or fighting for a seat on your commute, we need to make time for fun and play – enjoy the little things. Why not make funny noises to remind you to stop taking things seriously, or learn some silly jokes, just to tell when times get hard? They could make you or other people around you laugh!

When a hurdle pops up in life, it’s easy to get bogged down – but the way we recount events can impact on our resilience. Rather than see the negatives, look for the ironic moments and tell people about them! Why not write parodies in your spare time about events that take place to help you compartmentalise? Script what happened as if it was happening to a character rather than yourself. We all know that some things in life aren’t fair. But take those events and send them up a bit in your scripts! Sometimes life needs a bit of a roasting to get your thoughts in order, and embracing your comedic side, seeing life’s difficult moments as obstacles that can be made fun of rather than overwhelm you, may help you get through them more easily. And who knows, you may just discover a talent for writing at the end of it.

vocabulary.entry: blindside /ˈblaɪndsaɪd/ v. 出其不意地攻击；使措手不及
vocabulary.example: The sudden resignation of the CEO blindsided the entire company.
vocabulary.translation: 首席执行官的突然辞职让整个公司都措手不及。

vocabulary.entry: inopportune /ɪnˈɒpətjuːn/ adj. 不合时宜的；时机不当的
vocabulary.example: The phone call came at an inopportune moment during the meeting.
vocabulary.translation: 电话在会议开到一半的尴尬时刻打了进来。

vocabulary.entry: psyche /ˈsaɪki/ n. 心理；精神
vocabulary.example: The traumatic experience left a deep mark on her psyche.
vocabulary.translation: 这次创伤性经历在她的心理上留下了深深的烙印。

vocabulary.entry: therapeutic /ˌθerəˈpjuːtɪk/ adj. 治疗的；具有治愈作用的
vocabulary.example: Gardening can be a therapeutic activity for people with anxiety.
vocabulary.translation: 园艺对焦虑人群来说是一项具有治愈作用的活动。

vocabulary.entry: mundane /ˈmʌndeɪn/ adj. 单调的；平淡无奇的
vocabulary.example: She was tired of the mundane routine of her office job.
vocabulary.translation: 她厌倦了办公室工作的单调日常。

vocabulary.entry: arbitrary /ˈɑːbɪtrəri/ adj. 任意的；随心所欲的
vocabulary.example: The decision to increase prices seemed arbitrary and unfair.
vocabulary.translation: 涨价的决定看起来既随意又不公平。

vocabulary.entry: commute /kəˈmjuːt/ n. 通勤路程；上下班往返
vocabulary.example: Her daily commute takes about 45 minutes by train.
vocabulary.translation: 她每天坐火车通勤大约需要45分钟。

vocabulary.entry: hurdle /ˈhɜːdl/ n. 障碍；难关
vocabulary.example: Lack of funding is the main hurdle for the new project.
vocabulary.translation: 资金短缺是这个新项目的主要障碍。

vocabulary.entry: bog down /bɒɡ daʊn/ v. 使陷入困境；停滞不前
vocabulary.example: The negotiations were bogged down by technical details.
vocabulary.translation: 谈判因技术细节问题陷入了僵局。

vocabulary.entry: recount /rɪˈkaʊnt/ v. 讲述；叙述
vocabulary.example: She recounted her adventure in the jungle to her eager listeners.
vocabulary.translation: 她向热切的听众讲述了自己在丛林中的冒险经历。

vocabulary.entry: resilience /rɪˈzɪliəns/ n. 韧性；适应力
vocabulary.example: Children often show remarkable resilience after facing difficulties.
vocabulary.translation: 孩子们在遭遇困境后往往会表现出惊人的韧性。

vocabulary.entry: ironic /aɪˈrɒnɪk/ adj. 讽刺的；具有讽刺意味的
vocabulary.example: It's ironic that the firefighter's house burned down last night.
vocabulary.translation: 消防员的房子昨晚被烧毁了，这真是件极具讽刺意味的事。

vocabulary.entry: parody /ˈpærədi/ n. 戏仿作品；滑稽模仿之作
vocabulary.example: The film is a hilarious parody of classic spy movies.
vocabulary.translation: 这部电影是对经典间谍片的滑稽戏仿，十分搞笑。

vocabulary.entry: compartmentalise /ˌkɒmpɑːtˈmentəlaɪz/ v. 划分；分类处理
vocabulary.example: She learned to compartmentalise her work and personal life to reduce stress.
vocabulary.translation: 她学会了划分工作和个人生活，以减轻压力。

vocabulary.entry: script /skrɪpt/ v. 写剧本；编剧本
vocabulary.example: The writer was hired to script a new drama series for the TV channel.
vocabulary.translation: 这位作家受聘为电视台编写一部新的电视剧剧本。

vocabulary.entry: send up /send ʌp/ v. 嘲讽；挖苦
vocabulary.example: The comedian sent up the politician's mannerisms in his act.
vocabulary.translation: 这位喜剧演员在表演中嘲讽了那位政客的举止。

vocabulary.entry: roast /rəʊst/ n. 吐槽；调侃
vocabulary.example: The celebrity agreed to attend the charity roast for a good cause.
vocabulary.translation: 这位名人同意出席这场慈善吐槽大会，支持公益事业。

vocabulary.entry: comedic /kəˈmiːdɪk/ adj. 喜剧的；滑稽的
vocabulary.example: The actor's comedic timing is perfect, making every joke land.
vocabulary.translation: 这位演员的喜剧节奏把握得恰到好处，每个笑话都能引人发笑。

vocabulary.entry: obstacle /ˈɒbstəkl/ n. 障碍；阻碍
vocabulary.example: Poor eyesight was never an obstacle to her passion for reading.
vocabulary.translation: 视力不佳从未成为她热爱阅读的阻碍。

vocabulary.entry: overwhelm /ˌəʊvəˈwelm/ v. 压倒；使不知所措
vocabulary.example: She was overwhelmed by the amount of work she had to do.
vocabulary.translation: 堆积如山的工作让她感到手足无措。

vocabulary.entry: talent /ˈtælənt/ n. 天赋；才能
vocabulary.example: He has a natural talent for playing the piano.
vocabulary.translation: 他天生就有弹钢琴的天赋。

vocabulary.entry: toll /təʊl/ n. （身心的）损耗；代价
vocabulary.example: Years of hard work took a toll on his health.
vocabulary.translation: 多年的辛勤工作损害了他的健康。

vocabulary.entry: grin and bear /ɡrɪn ənd beə/ v. 默默忍受；逆来顺受
vocabulary.example: He had to grin and bear the unfair criticism from his boss.
vocabulary.translation: 他不得不默默忍受老板不公正的批评。

vocabulary.entry: suffer in silence /ˈsʌfə ɪn ˈsaɪləns/ v. 默默忍受痛苦
vocabulary.example: She suffered in silence for years before seeking help for her depression.
vocabulary.translation: 她默默忍受了多年抑郁的痛苦，才去寻求帮助。

vocabulary.entry: get down /ɡet daʊn/ v. 使沮丧；使情绪低落
vocabulary.example: Don't let the bad news get you down; things will get better.
vocabulary.translation: 别让坏消息影响你的心情，一切都会好起来的。

sentences.english: Sometimes life doesn’t seem to play fair.
sentences.chinese: 有时候生活似乎并不公平。

sentences.english: It blindsides you at the most inopportune moments, and even if we can learn to grin and bear the ups and downs, they can take their toll on our psyche.
sentences.chinese: 它总在最不合时宜的时刻出其不意地打击我们，即便我们能学默默承受人生的起起落落，这些经历也会对我们的心理造成伤害。

sentences.english: So rather than suffer in silence or let these things get you down, maybe there is another way: what if humour can help you get through the dark times?
sentences.chinese: 所以，与其默默承受痛苦，或是任由这些事情击垮自己，或许还有另一种办法：用幽默来帮你度过低谷期会怎么样呢？

sentences.english: According to author and clinician Kristen Lee: “Laughter and tears are both therapeutic – we need both to process such hard times.”
sentences.chinese: 作家兼临床医师克里斯汀·李表示：“欢笑与泪水都具有治愈功能——面对艰难时刻，我们需要二者兼备才能消化那些情绪。”

sentences.english: But how can we find the tough things that happen funny?
sentences.chinese: 但我们该如何从糟糕的事情中找到笑点呢？

sentences.english: Our lives are really serious, often filled with mundane and repetitive activities, whether it’s arbitrary bill paying or fighting for a seat on your commute, we need to make time for fun and play – enjoy the little things.
sentences.chinese: 生活本就十分严肃，还常常充斥着单调重复的琐事，无论是毫无理由地付账单，还是通勤时抢座位，我们都需要挤出时间自娱自乐——享受生活中的小确幸。

sentences.english: Why not make funny noises to remind you to stop taking things seriously, or learn some silly jokes, just to tell when times get hard?
sentences.chinese: 不妨试着弄出些搞怪的声响来提醒自己别把一切都看得太严肃，或者学几个无聊的笑话，专门在境遇不顺的时候讲出来。

sentences.english: They could make you or other people around you laugh!
sentences.chinese: 这些小举动说不定能让你自己，或是身边的人开怀一笑！

sentences.english: When a hurdle pops up in life, it’s easy to get bogged down – but the way we recount events can impact on our resilience.
sentences.chinese: 当生活中出现难关时，人很容易陷入困顿——但我们讲述经历的方式，会影响自身的心理韧性。

sentences.english: Rather than see the negatives, look for the ironic moments and tell people about them!
sentences.chinese: 与其只盯着消极的一面，不如去发掘那些充满讽刺意味的瞬间，讲给别人听！

sentences.english: Why not write parodies in your spare time about events that take place to help you compartmentalise?
sentences.chinese: 闲暇时，何不为发生过的事情写一些戏仿作品，帮助自己梳理情绪呢？

sentences.english: Script what happened as if it was happening to a character rather than yourself.
sentences.chinese: 把所经历的事情写成剧本，就当这些事发生在某个角色身上，而非你自己。

sentences.english: We all know that some things in life aren’t fair.
sentences.chinese: 我们都知道，生活中有些事本就不公平。

sentences.english: But take those events and send them up a bit in your scripts!
sentences.chinese: 但不妨把这些事写进剧本里调侃一番！

sentences.english: Sometimes life needs a bit of a roasting to get your thoughts in order, and embracing your comedic side, seeing life’s difficult moments as obstacles that can be made fun of rather than overwhelm you, may help you get through them more easily.
sentences.chinese: 有时候，生活需要被“吐槽”一番，才能理清思绪。展现自己幽默的一面，把生活中的困境看作可以拿来打趣的障碍，而非压垮自己的重担，或许能让你更轻松地度过难关。

sentences.english: And who knows, you may just discover a talent for writing at the end of it.
sentences.chinese: 谁知道呢，说不定最后你还能发掘出自己的写作天赋呢。
